responseText: {"title":"Two Eyes, Two Moods","question":"What does a face tell us when its two eyes refuse to agree?","introduction":"Every face here carries a visible split: two eye zones built from different shapes, different systems, different visual weights. Some differences are subtle — a slight size gap, a shift in height. Others are total opposites. Moving through this gallery, notice how that single asymmetry changes what the whole face seems to be doing, and whether a mouth full of teeth settles the question or opens a new one.","closing":"Fifteen faces, thirty eyes, none of them matched. Whether that asymmetry reads as unease, alertness, or something else may depend entirely on which eye you look at first.","chapters":[{"title":"Unequal but Contained","introduction":"These faces hold their asymmetry inside a stable structure. The two eye zones differ, but the overall form stays composed — the split is present without tipping into disorder.","stops":[{"slot":"W034","whyHere":"Two eye zones with different internal rhythms — one coiled, one cross-hatched — sit within a tightly stacked, slab-like form that keeps the tension compressed.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W074","whyHere":"A red grid appears over both eye zones, yet warm gold and cool teal beneath them give each side a different temperature, splitting the face through color rather than shape.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where W034 uses line density to separate its eyes, here the same structural device — a grid — lands on opposite color fields, making the split quieter but just as persistent."},{"slot":"W037","whyHere":"One eye is a warm concentric oval; the other is a cold rectangular box packed with scribbles. The near-black ground holds both in place without resolving the difference.","transitionFromPrevious":"W074 splits its eyes through color zones; W037 splits through geometry — circle versus rectangle — while a dark ground absorbs the friction rather than amplifying it."}]},{"title":"Radiating Against Winding","introduction":"Here the asymmetry becomes structural: one eye expands outward through rings or petals, the other contracts inward through spirals. The two eyes operate on opposite visual logics.","stops":[{"slot":"W018","whyHere":"A sunflower-like eye radiates orange petals outward on the right; a tight black-and-brown spiral winds inward on the left. The head feels pulled in two directions at once.","transitionFromPrevious":"W037's rectangular versus oval split gives way here to a more dynamic opposition: one eye that opens and one that closes, both set against a dense, pressured head mass."},{"slot":"W106","whyHere":"Concentric spoked rings expand from the left eye while dense parallel bars compress the right into a tight column — the most explicit outward-versus-inward opposition in the gallery.","transitionFromPrevious":"W018 pairs a petal-burst with a spiral; W106 sharpens the contrast to spokes against bars, making the two visual systems feel almost mechanical in their opposition."},{"slot":"W079","whyHere":"A single large spiral eye dominates the center while the left side holds a rectangular zone of magenta and yellow — one eye pulls inward, the other zone pushes outward in flat color.","transitionFromPrevious":"W106 balances its two opposing eyes symmetrically in the frame; W079 lets the spiral eye overwhelm the composition, making the asymmetry a matter of scale as much as form."},{"slot":"W081","whyHere":"The left eye is a wide white circle on black — open and staring — while the right coils into a white spiral. The asymmetry here is not just between left and right but between presence and void.","stops":[{"slot":"W044","whyHere":"Three eye-like forms appear: two looping ovals on the left and one larger tilted almond on the right, cooler and more open — the face exceeds the expected pair entirely.","transitionFromPrevious":"W081's two mismatched eyes are still recognizably a pair; W044 adds a third form, making the count itself part of the asymmetry."},{"slot":"W022","whyHere":"One eye swells to fill nearly a quarter of the image; the other shrinks to a small dark circle.
